s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy
key_facts: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
patient was being treated with fluconazole
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped 3 months prior due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction
patient has fever and hypotension
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative

shortlist.label: intravascular large b cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy findings showing intravascular atypical cells

shortlist.label: erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: patient has a history of morbilliform reaction and new skin eruption

shortlist.label: vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has fever, hypotension, and rash

shortlist.label: mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis and new skin eruption

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, as shown by hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, is a key diagnostic feature of intravascular large B cell lymphoma, which explains the patient's widespread skin eruption, fever, and hypotension.

rejected.label: erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The new skin eruption appeared different from the previous morbilliform reaction, and the presence of atypical cells on biopsy does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has a skin eruption, the biopsy findings of intravascular atypical cells are more consistent with a lymphoma than vasculitis.

rejected.label: mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The patient's skin eruption and biopsy findings do not typically match those of mycosis fungoides, which often presents with more specific skin lesions and epidermotropism.

rejected.label: febrile illness
rejected.why: This is a non-specific diagnosis that does not account for the patient's specific skin and biopsy findings.
